title: Christian Doppler: Why an Ambulance Siren Changes Pitch | Born 223 Years Ago Today

lines: Why does a siren change its sound as it passes you? The answer comes from him!
Who changed the world today? November 29.

lines: His family had been stonemasons for generations.
But he was a frail boy, too weak to haul heavy stone.
So his father sent him to school instead,
and he turned out to be brilliant at math.
As a young man, he couldn't find a teaching job anywhere.
In 1835, he sold his things and set off to emigrate to America.
In eighteen thirty-five, he sold his things and set off to emigrate to America.
Just before he left, a job offer came from Prague.
He stayed, and his life took a new turn.
In 1842, in Prague, he presented a bold idea:
In eighteen forty-two, in Prague, he presented a bold idea:
Moving toward you, waves bunch up: the pitch rises.
when something moves toward you, its waves bunch up, and the pitch goes higher;
Moving away, waves stretch out: the pitch drops.
when it moves away, the waves stretch out, and the pitch goes lower.
He said starlight works the same way.
In 1845, a Dutch scientist put it to the test.
In eighteen forty-five, a Dutch scientist put it to the test.
He had trumpet players stand on a train and play one steady note.
As the train came closer, the note rose; as it left, it fell.
Doppler was right!
He died of illness in Venice in 1853, at just forty-nine.
He died of illness in Venice in eighteen fifty-three, at just forty-nine.
Today, weather radar, speed guns and hospital ultrasound,
even measuring how distant galaxies move, all use his idea.
His question for you:
Is there something you hear every day, but never asked why?
